report:
Reviewed the complete dependency claim and all five ordinary implementation associations in resolve/mod.rs, resolve/ribs.rs, and symbol/mod.rs, plus the sole associated TODO test. Additional local module expansion/completeness source is captured as a dependency. This remains explicitly test-TODO: no passing no-op is treated as dependency or incremental-reuse evidence.

The requirements are that lookup observes searched lexical/module scopes and external membership keys, provider discovery produces identities before selected signatures are loaded, and resolution does not read checked bodies. Ribs::lookup only examines the current in-memory scope stack in reverse precedence order. Resolver::resolve_path returns a rib hit before module lookup; relative multi-segment and anchored paths follow selected module/enum children, and fallback preludes are searched only after the preceding bucket is empty. resolve_name_from_module tracks module/name/namespace in-flight keys to avoid recursive imports and selects the phase-appropriate bucket. The owning phase therefore acquires dependencies through the lookup branches it actually traverses. The new import_root_is_expansion_ambiguous audit deliberately reads generated named candidates and, only when present, competing glob routes; these are necessary scopes for that separate ambiguity check, not unconditional dependencies added to every normal lookup. It uses span provenance/identity and does not demand signatures or checked bodies.

Symbol::expanded_module_items dispatches to local expanded membership or external module membership. SymExt::named_children is a tracked lookup keyed by external symbol, name, and namespace; it filters raw exported edges before creating matching identities. Its underlying module_children access is module membership rather than a checked body or an unrelated function signature. SymExt::trait_children similarly enumerates trait identities from external membership without signatures. Resolver::traits_in_method_scope first collects local/imported/prelude trait identities and completeness flags; it does not call trait or function signature lowering. The unrelated signature accessor methods in symbol/mod.rs are separate operations, not calls made by these identity enumeration paths. Captured local expansion code explains that module enumeration may require macro resolution/expansion and completeness traversal of relevant providers; this is not checked-function-body evaluation. Macro body tokens needed to expand declarations are distinct from checked bodies. No checked-body call appears in the reviewed resolution paths.

The only associated test, semantic_spec::todo::resolution_lookup_dependencies, explicitly defers cold/warm query traces, exact scope and external-key assertions, exclusions of unrelated modules/signatures/checked bodies, and reuse after unrelated edits. It covers every empirical dimension still missing: source inspection cannot prove absence of hidden query dependencies or incremental reuse. Completing this anchor requires instrumented traced fixtures exercising hits, fallbacks, import cycles, provider discovery, and edits to unrelated inputs. This accepted deferral retains TODO status and does not certify the complete dependency guarantee as tested. There are no N/A entries. No new regression or additional implementation change was required by the reviewed import audit. This review executed start/read/record only; it makes no claim that a dependency trace test was run. The separately run lookup and macro behavioral tests are not substituted for such evidence.
